examples.title: Fake “Boss” Gift Card Request
examples.description: Call or message the person directly using a number or channel you already know is theirs, rather than replying to the email.

examples.title: Fake Benefits Enrollment Email
examples.description: Log into your company's actual HR or benefits portal directly to check your enrollment status, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake Cloud Storage Payment Failure
examples.description: Log into the real storage provider's site or app directly to check your billing status, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake Inheritance / Advance-Fee Letter
examples.description: Don't reply or engage — a stranger offering a fortune from nowhere is never real, no matter how detailed or emotional the story.

examples.title: Fake Retailer Survey Prize Email
examples.description: Check the retailer's real site or app directly for any active promotions, rather than clicking the link or the unsubscribe button.

examples.title: Fake PayPal Account Limited Email
examples.description: Type paypal.com directly into your browser and log in there to check your account status, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake Zoom Meeting Attendees Email
examples.description: Open the Zoom app directly to start or check a meeting, rather than clicking a meeting link from an unexpected email.

examples.title: Fake FedEx Shipping Confirmation Email
examples.description: Look up your tracking number directly on FedEx's real site or app, rather than clicking the link or code in the email.

examples.title: Fake Facebook Password Reset Email
examples.description: Go directly to facebook.com yourself to check or change your password, and never enter a reset code on a page you clicked to from an email.

examples.title: Fake Microsoft Missed Call Voicemail Email
examples.description: Don't open the attached file — if you weren't expecting a voicemail, verify through a phone system you already use before opening anything.

examples.title: Fake Health Insurer Survey Prize Email
examples.description: Check your real insurer's site or member portal directly for any active offers, rather than completing the survey or clicking the button.

examples.title: Fake McAfee Subscription Renewal Email
examples.description: Check your billing status by logging into your real McAfee account directly, rather than calling a number printed in the email.

examples.title: Fake W-2 / Amended Tax Form Email
examples.description: Check your actual tax documents through your employer's real payroll system or IRS.gov directly, not a link in an unexpected email.

examples.title: Fake Charity Tree-Planting Donation Email
examples.description: Look up the charity independently (e.g. through a charity-verification site) and donate directly through its real, verified website.

examples.title: Fake Microsoft 365 Security Alert Email
examples.description: Log into your Microsoft account directly through a browser you typed yourself to check recent sign-in activity, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake E-Invitation Email
examples.description: Confirm the party and host directly with someone you know before clicking an invitation link or button from an unexpected email.

examples.title: Fake Retailer Sweepstakes Winner Email
examples.description: If you don't remember entering, you didn't win anything — check the retailer's real site directly for any actual promotions.

examples.title: Fake Hacker Blackmail / Sextortion Email
examples.description: This is a mass-sent bluff with no real access to anything — don't pay, don't reply, and report it rather than engaging.

examples.title: Fake HR Shared Document Email
examples.description: Check your company's real HR portal or intranet directly for any organizational updates, instead of clicking the link.

examples.title: Fake Employee Gift Card Email
examples.description: Confirm any workplace reward program directly with your actual HR department before clicking a link to redeem anything.

examples.title: Fake DocuSign Document Signing Email
examples.description: Log into your real DocuSign account directly to check for pending documents, rather than clicking the link in the email.

examples.title: Fake High-Salary Job Offer Email
examples.description: Research the company and recruiter independently before responding, and never submit personal or financial details through an unsolicited job "application."

examples.title: Fake Google Drive Folder Share Email
examples.description: Check Google Drive directly by going to drive.google.com yourself, rather than clicking a link or button in the email.

examples.title: Fake QR Code Policy Review Email
examples.description: Don't scan unexpected QR codes — go directly to your real HR portal or intranet to review any company policy.
